heading: INT. FEDERAL COURTHOUSE - HOLDING CORRIDOR - DAY

units.text: INT. FEDERAL COURTHOUSE - HOLDING CORRIDOR - DAY
A narrow, windowless corridor behind the courtroom.
Cinder block painted the color of old teeth.
A bench bolted to the wall.
At one end a steel door with a buzzer.
At the other, a wall phone in a wire cage.
JUDGE PRUDENCE ADEKUNLE-WALSH, sixties, in her robe, stands in the doorway from chambers, tapping a gavel against her palm.
DEFENSE COUNSEL THEODORE MBATHA, forties, paces.
PROSECUTOR LUCINDA FAIRCLOUGH, thirties, sits on the bench with her briefcase on her knees.
The defendant, MR. SEBASTIAN OKORO-LANE, fifties, sits cuffed on the opposite end, rocking.
The court officer, DEPUTY MARCUS HOLLINGBERRY, forties, has a hand on his radio.
The wall phone rings.
Everyone freezes.
It rings again.
Lucinda lifts her head.
Theodore stops pacing.
Sebastian stops rocking.
Deputy Hollingberry unclips his radio and steps toward the phone.
Hold on.
units.name: HOLLINGBERRY

units.text: He lifts the receiver.
A tinny voice crackles.
Your Honor? We've reached a verdict. But we have a problem.
units.name: JUROR FOREPERSON

units.text: It's the jury. They've got a verdict.
units.name: HOLLINGBERRY

units.text: What problem?
units.name: JUDGE ADEKUNLE-WALSH

units.text: What problem?
units.name: HOLLINGBERRY

units.text: One of us is missing. Number nine. He went to the restroom forty minutes ago.
units.name: JUROR FOREPERSON

units.text: The group erupts at once.
Theodore swears.
Lucinda stands, her briefcase sliding off her knees.
The judge, unmoving, closes her eyes.
Sebastian slumps to the floor and mutters at the tile.
They lost a juror. They lost a juror.
units.name: SEBASTIAN

units.text: Your Honor, I move for a mistrial.
units.name: THEODORE

units.text: Your Honor, the state opposes. An alternate can be seated.
units.name: LUCINDA

units.text: Quiet. All of you. Quiet.
units.name: JUDGE ADEKUNLE-WALSH

units.text: The corridor falls silent.
The judge walks the length of it, robe swishing, and takes the phone out of the deputy's hand.
She listens for a moment.
Madam Foreperson, did anyone knock on the restroom door?
units.name: JUDGE ADEKUNLE-WALSH

units.text: Yes, Your Honor.
units.name: JUROR FOREPERSON

units.text: And?
units.name: JUDGE ADEKUNLE-WALSH

units.text: He knocked back.
units.name: JUROR FOREPERSON

units.text: The judge hangs up.
She hands the receiver to Hollingberry, turns to the corridor, and raises her gavel.
Then she lowers it and, quietly, to nobody, says:
Thirty years on the bench.
units.name: JUDGE ADEKUNLE-WALSH
